The full Rehatsek text was downloaded and read at the passage itself, not summarised: inside Story 10 of chapter I it prints The sons of Adam are limbs of each other / Having been created of one essence. / When the calamity of time afflicts one limb / The other limbs cannot remain at rest. The obvious attack was translation drift on line three, since the rendering that circulates most widely, including on Wikipedia's Bani Adam page, reads affects one limb, and a refuter working from memory would have called afflicts a slip. It is not: the scan reads afflicts, and the verifier was right to say so. Lineation, capitals at the line heads, the full stop after essence and the full stop after rest all match the page, and the cut at line four is clean because line five begins the conditional If you have no sympathy. Lines 1 to 4 is therefore an accurate count of the verse, which runs to six. THE DEFECT: Rehatsek's chapter I is titled The Manners of Kings. That is the title in the volume's contents (The Manners of Kings 23), in the list of the eight chapters in the prefatory matter (I. The Manners of Kings), in the chapter's own display heading (THE MANNERS OF KINGS), and in the running head on every recto of the chapter. On the Conduct of Kings is the title used by other English Gulistans, not by the translation the card names, so the source line puts a title in Rehatsek's mouth that he did not write. Under a confident false citation is worse than an honest attributed to, that is a refutation, and the fix is one clause: the betterCitation above, 107 characters, leads with the name, no dash. The 35 header precedes Story 10 and the four lines; the 36 header falls between line four and line five, so page 36 opens on If you have no sympathy for the troubles of others. Worse, that pagination is not the 1888 edition's at all: the file read is the Omphaloskepsis Books edition of 2010, edited by David Rosenbaum, which reprints Rehatsek's translation with its own page numbers. The evidence presents a 2010 reprint's page as the named 1888 edition's. No page number appears in the shipped source line, so nothing false reaches the card, but the evidence must not travel as it stands. Everything else clears.
